prompt:
feat(skills): lint every skill against the published specification (S44, ADR-069)

The specification was fetched rather than recalled, which changed the work:
the review listed three limits and the document has eight rules, including
the one that breaks an install - a name must equal the directory it lives
in, and the directory is created from the name, so an install that ignores
that rule deploys a skill no client can address by the name inside it.

What the specification calls a must fails the exit code; what it calls a
recommendation warns. A lint that fails on advice is a lint that gets
skipped.  asks the same name rules the lint enforces, from
the one place both read them.

The other thing reading the document caught: most real descriptions are
written as folded block scalars, and a reader that treats the arrow as the
value measured a 200-character description as two characters. The first run
of this lint said exactly that about five real skills before the reader was
rewritten.
f2p: a body past the recommended size is a warning that says what it costs
a description over the specification limit fails, and a short one is a warning
a description written as a folded block scalar is read as text, not as its arrow
a name that disagrees with its directory is the rule installs break on
a name the specification forbids fails with the rule it broke
compatibility has its own limit, and most skills do not need it
lintSpec checks the canonical source, and names the skill in every finding
the flat form is reported, because a client looks for SKILL.md by name
the specification is named, so a reader can check the claim
